title: Declarative tool composition API and ergonomics for parallel/serial calls
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Introduces a declarative composition surface for multi-tool and mixed parallel/serial invocation patterns and improves ergonomics for result injection, retry semantics, and OpenAI-compatibility behavior. Motivation: Current ad-hoc composition helpers mix imperative plumbing with model prompts in application code. This PR provides a small, typed composition DSL plus runtime helpers to make multi-tool call patterns easy to declare, test, and observe. Goals: 1) Expose a declarative API that lets callers express 'fanout then reduce' and 'sequential pipeline' patterns with minimal boilerplate. 2) Provide clear semantics for when tool results are injected into the model prompt vs returned separately. 3) Unify retry/backoff policy defaults and make them overrideable per-call and per-tool. 4) Preserve existing OpenAI-compat shim behavior but make opt-in toggles explicit.

Design highlights:
- New Composition spec (redwood.api.composition.CompositionSpec) — lightweight JSON-serializable structure: a list of steps where each step is either a parallel block (named tools run concurrently) or a serial step (single tool with optional input mapping). The runtime executes a graph but surface intentionally avoids arbitrary graph cycles to keep deterministic replay simple.
- Call surface: redwood.Client.compose(spec, context, options) returns a CompositionResult that contains per-step metadata (latency, retries, status) and an optional synthesized prompt used for streaming. By default the runtime does not inject tool outputs into the generation stream; callers can set inject_results: "inline" to stream tool outputs into the model tokens, or "separate" to keep them out-of-band.
- Retry semantics: per-tool retry_policy supports idempotent/at-most-once/at-least-once semantics plus max_attempts and jittered exponential backoff. The composition runner surfaced default policy aligned with our serving SLOs (short timeouts for latency-sensitive fanout, conservatively higher for background pipelines).
- OpenAI-compat: updates to the compat layer to support function_call semantics for composition steps. When a composition step maps to a function-like tool, we emit function_call events with structured arguments. For compatibility we provide config.auto_function_to_tool = true to map old function_call patterns into the new composition runtime.
- Observability: each CompositionResult includes a trace_id and annotated spans for batching, network, and model time. We wired these into console dashboards and added sample queries for common latency breakdowns.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Existing imperative helpers remain supported. compose() is additive; no existing API was removed.
- For users relying on previous implicit injection behavior, config.injection_default is set to "separate" to avoid unexpected model hallucination regressions; opt-in required to return to previous behavior.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests cover composition graph validation, mapping rules, and retry edge-cases.
- Integration tests simulate mixed parallel/serial flows against the OpenAI-compat shim and our hosted runtime with a canary rollout to 10% of traffic.
- Feature-flagged rollout: runtime flag composition.v1 enabled for 10% of requests in staging, then 50% in canary, then 100% after 72h with no regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] API surface and proto sketched
- [x] Implementation in runtime + client
- [x] OpenAI-compat mapping implemented
- [x] Observability wired into console traces
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Migration docs (docs/compose.md) added

Related: ENG-7312 (composition ergonomics), ENG-7451 (compat layer updates), SUP-2191 (customer reported mixed parallel calls issue).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This looks good overall. Concern: defaulting injection to 'separate' is safer, but we should provide a deprecation timeline if customers opt-in previously. Can we add telemetry to track how many calls use inline injection?
Maya Patel: Added telemetry counters (runtime/compose/injection_mode usage) in runner.py and documented in docs/compose.md. No deprecation planned until after 6 weeks of usage data.
Renee Zhao: Implementation detail: runner currently spawns a thread per parallel tool which could overwhelm small hosts. Can we use a shared worker pool or semaphore?
Maya Patel: Switched to a bounded async worker pool; updated tests. Added a fallback semaphore to prevent OOM on tiny nodes.
Diego Martinez: Are retry semantics observable per-tool in the console? If a tool retries 3x, we should surface the attempts and last_error.
Maya Patel: CompositionResult now includes attempts and last_error fields per step. Console queries updated.
Renee Zhao: Minor nit: rename CompositionSpec -> CompositionDefinition for clarity?
Maya Patel: Kept CompositionSpec to avoid churn with existing internal references; updated doc examples to make meaning clear.
CI Bot: flake8 and mypy initially failed on compose.py (typing gaps).
Maya Patel: Fixed typing, added stricter annotations and re-ran CI. All green now.
ci_checks: e2e: pass on staging with 10% rollout
merge_result: Merged by squash+merge after approvals from reviewers. Merge commit: squash(a1e7d82..f9d0e77). Release notes included in docs/compose.md.
release_notes: Add a new declarative composition API (compose) for expressing parallel and sequential tool invocation patterns. Defaults keep tool output separate from model streaming to avoid hallucination regressions. OpenAI-compat function_call mapping added and toggleable. Observability added for per-step latencies and retries.
notes_for_release_team: Enable composition.v1 in canary with 10% traffic; validate runtime.compose.injection_mode telemetry and dashboard panels. Coordinate with SDK maintainers to publish new client versions. Notify customer success for SUP-2191 follow-ups.
